title: Refactor Repeated Stimulus into a Task
description: Turn three copy-pasted stimulus blocks into one automatic task with arguments, remove a testbench drive race, and make the bench check its own results.

steps.title: Step 1: Run the starter and record the counts
steps.instructions: Compile work/dut_counter.sv together with work/tb_counter_unrefactored.sv, run the simulation and write down the three counts it prints. The starter drives enable with a blocking assignment (enable = 1) right after @(posedge clk), so it races the DUT's always_ff on the same edge: if the DUT runs first the counts are 6, 106 and 190, if the testbench runs first they are 4, 96 and 159. Note which edges race and why another simulator may print different numbers (README, step 1).

steps.title: Step 2: Write task automatic drive_sequence
steps.instructions: In work/tb_counter_unrefactored.sv, write task automatic drive_sequence(input byte start_value, input int unsigned repeat_count, input byte step = 8'h01). Declare byte payload = start_value; first. Wait for @(posedge clk), drive enable and data with <=, then on each of repeat_count clock edges add step to payload and drive it on data with <=. Finally clear enable with <=, wait one more edge and print the [Task] line. Explain why the payload initializer is legal only because the task is automatic.

steps.title: Step 3: Replace the three blocks with calls
steps.instructions: Replace the three copy-pasted scenarios with three calls: drive_sequence(8'h01, 3) uses the default step, drive_sequence(8'h10, 5, 8'h02) passes every argument by position, and drive_sequence(.start_value(8'h20), .repeat_count(8), .step(8'h03)) binds them by name. Run again: every simulator must now print the counts 6, 106 and 190.

steps.title: Step 4: Make the bench check itself
steps.instructions: Add a reference model: a variable exp_count that starts at 0 with the reset, and a function automatic that adds one burst's values (start_value, start_value + step, and so on, repeat_count of them) modulo 256. After each burst compare count !== exp_count, count passes and failures, report a failure with $error, and print PASS=<n> FAIL=<m> before $finish. Expect PASS=3 FAIL=0. Then change the DUT to count <= count + data + 1, confirm that FAIL is no longer 0, and undo the change.
